title: The Abandoned
full_review:
"The Abandoned" (Lionsgate/After Dark Films), Spanish director and co-writer Nacho Cerda's first feature-length movie, is standard horror fare with a modestly intriguing premise. Offering sufficient scares without any glaringly exploitative elements, it is ultimately hobbled by a lack of coherence.

Russian-born Marie (Anastasia Hille), now divorced and living in Los Angeles, goes back to her country in search of her birth parents and to learn about her early days.

Venturing to the remote and obviously haunted house in which she was born, and which hasn't been entered in 40-plus years, she has ominous visions and hears strange sounds.

Nikolai (Karel Roden) claiming to be her twin brother appears and they discover they each have zombie doppelgangers who don't wish them well. The past eventually erupts into the present when whoever brutally murdered their mother on the night of their first birthday comes back to finish the job. Can they alter the past or at least save themselves in the present?

Although the story is above-average for the genre, certain plot details, particularly during the confusing climax, don't withstand close scrutiny. Handsome shots of the surrounding countryside are offset by extremely jittery camera work inside the house, plus choppy editing and jarring sound effects.

The film contains violent and gory images, profanity, nudity, and one brief sequence in which a sex act is heard off-camera in a porn film. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
